# Optical diffraction: unregistered prototype status

The package is an additional candidate alongside the thirteen registered worlds.
It has no active shared score, agent service or GPT result. Numerical calibration
and pure coordinate policy checks are separate from registration.

The fixed author batch used six development instances, three disclosed generator
strata and a predeclared source/target design. It completed 61 World attempts
(60 valid), 73 production calls including their 60 nested solves, 29 independent
pair-formula calls and 36 public-record baseline predictions. Three deliberate
input/work/nonfinite guard failures were retained; no unexpected failure occurred.
The two-stage nesting must not be counted as independent physical experiments.
All predictions were sealed before target acquisition.

A separate six-case, 60-digit Decimal calculation checked 88 rows per side. The
maximum production discrepancy was 5.00e-16 against a fixed 5e-12 tolerance, with
no retries or threshold changes. This is finite numerical calibration of the
ideal scalar coherent model, not a uniform error bound or real-device validation.

The baseline uses the publicly supplied quadratic contrast identity and linear
interpolation of observed response against the absolute scattering coordinate.
On the same 72 target cells, its pooled clean-target RMSE was:

| Source scans | Within sampled coordinate range: 42 cells | Outside range: 30 cells |
|---|---:|---:|
| 0 | 0.666283 | 0.905417 |
| 1 | 0.420162 | 0.307216 |
| 3 | 0.000988 | 0.164512 |

The zero-source partition uses the proposed source grid as its reference range;
it does not imply that observations were available. Errors against independently
noisy targets at three scans were 0.002429 and 0.163774 respectively. Individual
regressions are retained: more source scans did not improve every query. The
large extrapolation error concerns an endpoint-hold baseline; it does not prove
that the world is intrinsically difficult. The low interpolation error does not
establish discovery of the supplied contrast law or unique hidden positions.

An exactly constructed pair of distinct point sets has the same full ordinary
intensity function. A specified endpoint-tag intervention separates that pair;
translation and reflection ambiguities remain. This is a useful identification
counterexample, not a theorem that all geometries become identifiable.

The public-coordinate helper is still isolated from shared evaluators. It keeps
informative zero-angle cells when contrast differs from one, excludes the exact
publicly assigned forward cell, and recognizes sign/wavelength reparameterizations
of the same absolute scattering coordinate. Eligibility is an administrative
policy, not proof of novelty, effect detectability or mechanism dependence.

Before registration, the shared score, claim, prospective-history and mapping
paths need versioned routing and their own integration review. Old time-axis
rules cannot simply be reused for angles. Historical thirteen-world contracts
and completed GPT scores are unchanged.

Independent-context scientific review is same-family/provisional, pending
external review, with no available integrity certification. Saved hashes and
ordered logs establish internal consistency under the trusted operator.
